title: "one creator, truth is the name"

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ik Onkar, the numeral one that opens the scripture. Today, the words that come right after it. Day ten.

Describe God in a single breath. Not a book, not a sermon: a few words, short enough for a child to memorize and deep enough for a lifetime. Right after the symbol for one, at the top of the scripture, Guru Nanak does exactly that. Sikhs call it the Mool Mantar, the root verse, and many say it every morning. Today, its first line.
screen: `DESCRIBE GOD IN ONE BREATH.` → `THE ROOT VERSE.` → `A SEED THAT HOLDS A TREE.`

segments.voice: Mool means root. Mantar is the Punjabi form of mantra, a sacred phrase. The scripture's language is centuries old, and even fluent Punjabi speakers look words up, so one line at a time is how everyone reads it. After Ik Onkar, it says: Sat Naam. Karta Purakh. Sat means truth, and something deeper than true as opposed to false: it comes from an old root meaning what really is, what lasts. Naam means name. Sat Naam: truth is the name, or the one whose name is truth. The Victorian scholar Max Arthur Macauliffe, who translated with Sikh scholars beside him, gave the opening as: "There is but one God whose name is true, the Creator." Here's the surprise in naam. On this path the name isn't just a label, like yours printed on a bill. It comes to mean the whole presence of God, running through everything. Then Karta Purakh. Karta, the maker. Purakh, the being. The creator: not a force that set the world going and walked away, but the one still making. Three ideas in five words: there is one, its name is truth, and it creates. And a quiet challenge inside: if truth is God's name, then telling the truth is a way of saying it.
screen: `MOOL MANTAR — THE ROOT VERSE.` · `SAT — WHAT REALLY IS.` · `NAAM — MORE THAN A LABEL.` · `KARTA PURAKH — THE ONE STILL MAKING.`

segments.voice: Breathe, and think of one true thing about your life right now: not the flattering version, just the true one. Sit with it without fixing it. If you like, let two words go out with the breath: Sat Naam.
The Mool Mantar, the root verse. Line one: Ik Onkar, Sat Naam, Karta Purakh. There is one, truth is the name, the creator. Tenth word.
Your line: the name is truth. Which makes an honest sentence a small way of saying it. Day ten.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite the Mool Mantar at the start of the morning prayer Japji Sahib and at many other times; it stands at the head of the Guru Granth Sahib and is often the first passage children memorize.

what it means: the first line of the root verse: there is one, truth is the name, the creator.
what a scholar hears: sat comes from an old root meaning being, what really exists. so Sat Naam can be heard as: the name is reality itself.
